newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA URGED TO JOIN GREENHOUSE GAS CLUB.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA URGED TO JOIN GREENHOUSE GAS CLUB.

text.p: A senior South African government official on Tuesday urged politicians to ratify the United Nations Convention on Climate Change so that the country could play a role in forming world policy on greenhouse gases.

Francois Hanekom, deputy director general in the department of the environment, told a parliamentary committee that South Africa with its coal-burning power stations was responsible for 1.6 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions.
"This makes us the largest source of emissions in Africa and the 18th largest in the world," he said.
South Africa is one of about 160 nations that have signed the convention but the country has yet to ratify it, which means it is exluded from negotiations on ways to combat global warming.
"We can no longer afford to be outside the main negotiating chambers... We plead that we must move in to use our positive influence," Hanekom said.

He added that South Africa would have to ratify the convention by the end of the month if it wanted to participate fully in the third conference of convention members due to be held in Japan in December.
He said South Africa's obligations under the convention would be negligible compared with the potential benefits.

"It becomes eligible as a developing country for grant funding... intended to cover the additional costs for developing countries on their investments towards these global environmental benefits," Hanekom said.
"As a developing country we cannot be forced into the commitments that will be placed on the developed sector who are being blamed for having done the major damage to the atmosphere."
Hanekom said that while some scientests contested the reality of global warming, South Africa supported the view that world temperatures could rise by up to 3.5 degress Celsius over the next century.
